quizQuestions.prompt: What condition did Leviticus require for an animal offered as a burnt offering?
quizQuestions.explanation: The animal had to be a male without blemish, a perfect offering to God.

quizQuestions.prompt: What offering did Leviticus prescribe when someone broke one of the LORD's commandments without meaning to?
quizQuestions.explanation: A sin offering atoned for sins committed unintentionally.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which land animals were considered clean for Israel to eat under the Law?
quizQuestions.explanation: Animals that chewed the cud and had a split hoof were clean to eat.

options.text: Those that chew the cud and have a split hoof

quizQuestions.prompt: On the Day of Atonement, what happened to the goat that carried away Israel's sins?
quizQuestions.explanation: The scapegoat was sent away into the wilderness, symbolically carrying Israel's sins away.

options.text: It was sent into the wilderness
It was kept in the tabernacle
It was given to the priests
It was set free in the camp

quizQuestions.prompt: Which command in Leviticus did Jesus later call one of the greatest commandments?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Love thy neighbour as thyself" was later affirmed by Jesus as a great commandment.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Leviticus 23, how many appointed feasts did God give Israel to keep?
quizQuestions.explanation: God appointed seven feasts: Passover, Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Weeks, Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and Tabernacles.

quizQuestions.prompt: How often did the Year of Jubilee occur?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Jubilee was proclaimed every fiftieth year.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened during the Year of Jubilee?
quizQuestions.explanation: Land was returned to its original owners and Israelite slaves were set free.

options.text: Land was returned and slaves were freed

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was ordained as Israel's first high priest in Leviticus?
quizQuestions.explanation: Aaron was anointed and ordained as high priest.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu after they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord?
quizQuestions.explanation: Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them for offering "strange fire."

options.text: Fire came from the Lord and consumed them
They were exiled from the camp
They were forgiven and continued serving
They lost their priesthood but lived

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Leviticus 26 promise Israel if they obeyed God's commands?
quizQuestions.explanation: God promised blessings, rain, harvest, and peace for obedience.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was responsible for examining and diagnosing skin diseases like leprosy under the Law?
quizQuestions.explanation: The priest examined those with suspected skin disease.

quizQuestions.prompt: What principle of justice did Leviticus 24 describe for injuries?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Eye for eye, tooth for tooth" described proportional justice.

options.text: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Leviticus, to whom does the tithe of the land belong?
quizQuestions.explanation: The tithe of the land is holy, belonging to the Lord.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Leviticus 17:11, what did God say is "in the blood"?
quizQuestions.explanation: God said the life of the flesh is in the blood, the basis for atonement through sacrifice.

quizQuestions.prompt: Where did Moses take a census of the Israelite men able to go to war?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses numbered the people in the wilderness of Sinai.

quizQuestions.prompt: How many spies did Moses send to explore the land of Canaan?
quizQuestions.explanation: Twelve spies, one from each tribe, were sent to scout Canaan.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which two spies gave a faithful, positive report about conquering Canaan?
quizQuestions.explanation: Caleb and Joshua alone urged Israel to trust God and take the land.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why did Israel wander in the wilderness for forty years?
quizQuestions.explanation: Their unbelief and refusal to enter Canaan led to forty years of wandering.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Korah and his followers after they rebelled against Moses' leadership?
quizQuestions.explanation: The earth opened and swallowed Korah, his household, and his followers.

options.text: The earth opened and swallowed them

quizQuestions.prompt: What miraculous sign confirmed Aaron as God's chosen priest?
quizQuestions.explanation: Aaron's staff budded, blossomed, and produced almonds overnight.

options.text: His rod budded and bore almonds
Fire fell from heaven on him

quizQuestions.prompt: Why was Moses forbidden from entering the Promised Land?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it as God commanded, failing to honor God as holy before Israel.

options.text: He struck the rock instead of speaking to it

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Moses lift up on a pole to heal those bitten by venomous snakes?
quizQuestions.explanation: A bronze serpent on a pole healed anyone who looked at it in faith.

quizQuestions.prompt: What animal spoke to the prophet Balaam?
quizQuestions.explanation: Balaam's donkey spoke to him after seeing the angel of the Lord blocking the road.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which king hired Balaam to curse Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Balak, king of Moab, hired Balaam, but Balaam ended up blessing Israel instead.

quizQuestions.prompt: What mountain did God tell Moses to climb to view the Promised Land before his death?
quizQuestions.explanation: God told Moses to go up Mount Abarim to see the land he would not enter.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who did God appoint to succeed Moses as leader of Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Joshua was appointed and commissioned by the laying on of hands.

quizQuestions.prompt: What well-known blessing did God give Aaron to pronounce over Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee..." is the priestly blessing given to Aaron.

options.text: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee"

quizQuestions.prompt: What food did God send to satisfy the Israelites' complaint for meat in the wilderness?
quizQuestions.explanation: God sent quail to feed the people who craved meat.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Miriam after she and Aaron spoke against Moses?
quizQuestions.explanation: Miriam was struck with leprosy for a time as a consequence.

quizQuestions.prompt: What large piece of fruit did the spies carry back from the Valley of Eshcol as evidence of the land's fruitfulness?
quizQuestions.explanation: A single cluster of grapes was so large it took two men to carry it on a pole.

quizQuestions.prompt: What guided the Israelites, telling them when to move camp and when to stay, throughout the wilderness journey?
quizQuestions.explanation: A cloud by day and fire by night rested over the tabernacle to guide Israel's movements.

options.text: The cloud and fire over the tabernacle

quizQuestions.prompt: Where did Aaron die and pass the priesthood to his son Eleazar?
quizQuestions.explanation: Aaron died on Mount Hor, where his priestly garments were placed on Eleazar.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is the great commandment Moses gave Israel in Deuteronomy 6, later called the Shema?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD... love the LORD thy God with all thine heart."

options.text: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God is one LORD"

quizQuestions.prompt: From what mountain did Moses view the Promised Land before he died?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses viewed Canaan from Mount Nebo, across the Jordan from Jericho.

quizQuestions.prompt: Where did Moses die?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses died in the land of Moab, buried by God in an unknown place.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Deuteronomy, no prophet since has risen in Israel like whom?
quizQuestions.explanation: "There arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses."

quizQuestions.prompt: What verse from Deuteronomy did Jesus later quote when tempted by Satan in the wilderness, about man not living by bread alone?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD."

options.text: "Man doth not live by bread only"

quizQuestions.prompt: What set of laws does Moses repeat to the new generation of Israel in Deuteronomy 5?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses restates the Ten Commandments to the generation about to enter Canaan.

quizQuestions.prompt: In Deuteronomy 18:15, Moses foretold that God would raise up a prophet like whom?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The LORD thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet... like unto me" — a prophecy pointing forward.

quizQuestions.prompt: What two things does Deuteronomy 28 set before Israel depending on obedience or disobedience?
quizQuestions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28 lists extensive blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience.

quizQuestions.prompt: What words of encouragement did Moses give Joshua and Israel before his death?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Be strong and of a good courage... the LORD thy God, he will not fail thee."

options.text: "Be strong and of a good courage"

quizQuestions.prompt: How old was Moses when he died?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses was 120 years old, his eye not dim nor his natural force abated.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Deuteronomy 6, when were the Israelites told to teach God's commandments to their children?
quizQuestions.explanation: They were told to teach continually — sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up.

quizQuestions.prompt: What written document did the Law of Moses require for a divorce?
quizQuestions.explanation: A bill (certificate) of divorcement was required.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to debts among Israelites every seventh year, according to Deuteronomy 15?
quizQuestions.explanation: Every seventh year, debts owed by fellow Israelites were released.

options.text: They were transferred to the priests
They were forgiven only for the poor

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Deuteronomy 17 require of any king Israel would later choose?
quizQuestions.explanation: The king had to be an Israelite chosen by God, not a foreigner.

options.text: He must be an Israelite chosen by God
He must be from the tribe of Levi
He must be chosen by lottery
He must be the oldest man in Israel

quizQuestions.prompt: From which two mountains were Israel's blessings and curses pronounced after entering Canaan?
quizQuestions.explanation: Blessings were pronounced from Mount Gerizim, curses from Mount Ebal.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Moses do for each of the twelve tribes of Israel just before he died?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses blessed each of the twelve tribes in Deuteronomy 33.

options.text: He appointed a king for each

quizQuestions.prompt: Where did Moses deliver his final speeches recorded in Deuteronomy?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses spoke to Israel on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Moses compose and teach Israel shortly before his death, calling heaven and earth as witnesses?
quizQuestions.explanation: Moses wrote and taught Israel a song, recorded in Deuteronomy 32.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who did God appoint to lead Israel into the Promised Land after Moses died?
quizQuestions.explanation: Joshua, Moses' assistant, was commissioned to lead Israel into Canaan.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who hid the Israelite spies in Jericho and helped them escape?
quizQuestions.explanation: Rahab hid the two spies on her roof and helped them escape the city.

quizQuestions.prompt: What sign did Rahab hang in her window so her family would be spared?
quizQuestions.explanation: A scarlet cord marked her window as the sign of the spies' promise.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Israel cross the Jordan River into Canaan?
quizQuestions.explanation: The waters stopped as priests carrying the ark stepped into the river, and Israel crossed on dry ground.

options.text: On dry ground, the waters were stopped

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to the walls of Jericho after Israel marched around it and shouted?
quizQuestions.explanation: The walls fell down flat, and Israel took the city.

quizQuestions.prompt: How many days did Israel march around Jericho before its walls fell?
quizQuestions.explanation: Israel marched once daily for six days, then seven times on the seventh day.

quizQuestions.prompt: Whose sin of taking forbidden plunder from Jericho caused Israel's defeat at Ai?
quizQuestions.explanation: Achan secretly kept silver, gold, and a garment devoted to destruction.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Joshua ask God to make stand still during the battle at Gibeon?
quizQuestions.explanation: Joshua asked for the sun and moon to stand still until Israel finished the battle.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which faithful spy asked for and received Hebron as his inheritance in his old age?
quizQuestions.explanation: Caleb, at 85, asked for the hill country because he wholly followed the Lord.

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous declaration did Joshua make to Israel near the end of his life?
quizQuestions.explanation: "As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."

options.text: "As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD"

quizQuestions.prompt: What did God tell Joshua to meditate on day and night so he would prosper?
quizQuestions.explanation: God told Joshua the Book of the Law should not depart from his mouth.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who appeared to Joshua near Jericho, identifying himself as captain of the LORD's host?
quizQuestions.explanation: A man with a drawn sword appeared, identifying himself as captain of the Lord's army.

options.text: A man with a drawn sword

quizQuestions.prompt: Which people tricked Joshua into making a peace treaty by disguising themselves as travelers from a far country?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Gibeonites deceived Israel with worn-out clothes and moldy bread.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Joshua set up at Gilgal as a memorial of Israel's crossing of the Jordan?
quizQuestions.explanation: Twelve stones, one for each tribe, were set up as a lasting memorial.

quizQuestions.prompt: How was the Promised Land divided among the tribes of Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: The land was divided among the tribes by casting lots.

options.text: By a vote of the elders

quizQuestions.prompt: What special cities did Joshua establish where someone who killed a person accidentally could flee for safety?
quizQuestions.explanation: Cities of refuge protected the accidental manslayer from revenge until a fair trial.

quizQuestions.prompt: What military strategy did Joshua use to finally conquer the city of Ai?
quizQuestions.explanation: Joshua set an ambush behind the city after the earlier defeat caused by Achan's sin.

quizQuestions.prompt: What time of year was it, causing the Jordan to be at flood stage, when God stopped its waters for Israel to cross?
quizQuestions.explanation: It was harvest time, when the Jordan overflowed its banks.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which tribes settled on the east side of the Jordan, before the conquest of Canaan was even finished?
quizQuestions.explanation: Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh chose land east of the Jordan.

options.text: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh

quizQuestions.prompt: How old was Joshua when he died?
quizQuestions.explanation: Joshua died at the age of 110.

quizQuestions.prompt: What repeating pattern do the events of the book of Judges follow?
quizQuestions.explanation: Israel sins, is oppressed, cries out to God, and He raises up a judge to deliver them.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was the prophetess and judge who led Israel and summoned Barak to battle?
quizQuestions.explanation: Deborah judged Israel and called Barak to lead the army against Sisera.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who killed the enemy commander Sisera by driving a tent peg through his head?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jael killed Sisera while he slept in her tent.

quizQuestions.prompt: What sign did Gideon ask God for to confirm his call to save Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Gideon asked for dew on the fleece, then dry fleece with dew on the ground.

options.text: Dew on a fleece of wool

quizQuestions.prompt: How many men did God leave Gideon with to defeat the Midianites, after reducing his army?
quizQuestions.explanation: God narrowed Gideon's army down to 300 men to make clear the victory was His.

quizQuestions.prompt: What unusual weapons did Gideon's 300 men use to rout the Midianite army?
quizQuestions.explanation: They used trumpets, empty pitchers, and torches to confuse and scatter the enemy.

quizQuestions.prompt: What vow set Samson apart from birth, including never cutting his hair?
quizQuestions.explanation: Samson was dedicated as a Nazirite from birth.

quizQuestions.prompt: What animal did Samson kill with his bare hands on the way to Timnah?
quizQuestions.explanation: Samson tore apart a young lion with his bare hands.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who discovered the secret of Samson's strength and betrayed him to the Philistines?
quizQuestions.explanation: Delilah persistently pressed Samson until he revealed his hair was the secret.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Samson die, defeating the Philistines one final time?
quizQuestions.explanation: Samson pushed down the temple's pillars, collapsing it on himself and the Philistines inside.

options.text: He pushed down the temple pillars
He was struck by an arrow

quizQuestions.prompt: Which left-handed judge killed Eglon, the king of Moab, with a hidden dagger?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ehud used his left hand to conceal and deliver a fatal blow to Eglon.

quizQuestions.prompt: What repeated phrase describes the moral state of Israel throughout the book of Judges?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Every man did that which was right in his own eyes," since there was no king in Israel.

options.text: "Every man did that which was right in his own eyes"
"There was peace for a thousand years"

quizQuestions.prompt: Which judge made a rash vow to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first, if God gave him victory?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jephthah made a costly vow before defeating the Ammonites.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Gideon's son Abimelech die, after making himself king by force?
quizQuestions.explanation: A woman dropped a millstone on his head during a siege.

options.text: A woman dropped a millstone on his head

quizQuestions.prompt: What unusual weapon did Samson use to kill a thousand Philistines?
quizQuestions.explanation: Samson used the jawbone of a donkey.

quizQuestions.prompt: What name did Gideon give the altar he built after the Lord called him "peace"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Gideon named the altar Jehovah-shalom, meaning "The LORD is peace."

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Israel fail to fully do to the Canaanite peoples after Joshua's death, according to Judges?
quizQuestions.explanation: Israel failed to drive them out completely, leaving them to dwell among the tribes.

options.text: Convert them to worship the LORD

quizQuestions.prompt: What did the Philistines do to Samson after Delilah's betrayal, before he pushed down the temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: They put out his eyes and bound him to grind grain at a mill.

options.text: Put out his eyes and bound him
Sold him as a slave to Moab

quizQuestions.prompt: What word did the Gileadites use to identify fleeing Ephraimites, since they couldn't pronounce it correctly?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Shibboleth" was used as a test of pronunciation at the fords of the Jordan.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why did Deborah tell Barak that the honor of defeating Sisera would go to a woman, not to him?
quizQuestions.explanation: Barak insisted Deborah go with him into battle instead of trusting God's word alone.

options.text: Because Barak insisted Deborah go with him
Because Barak refused to fight at all

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous pledge of loyalty did Ruth make to her mother-in-law Naomi?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Whither thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God."

quizQuestions.prompt: What nationality was Ruth before she joined Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ruth was a Moabite woman who chose to follow Naomi and Naomi's God.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was the name of Ruth's mother-in-law?
quizQuestions.explanation: Naomi was Ruth's mother-in-law, who she chose to stay with.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was the name of Ruth's sister-in-law who chose to stay in Moab instead of following Naomi?
quizQuestions.explanation: Orpah kissed Naomi goodbye and returned to her own people.

quizQuestions.prompt: In whose field did Ruth glean leftover grain to provide for herself and Naomi?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ruth gleaned in the field belonging to Boaz.

quizQuestions.prompt: What role did Boaz have that allowed him to eventually marry Ruth and redeem the family's land?
quizQuestions.explanation: Boaz was a close relative with the legal right and responsibility to redeem — a kinsman-redeemer.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was the name of the son born to Boaz and Ruth?
quizQuestions.explanation: Their son was named Obed.

quizQuestions.prompt: Ruth became the great-grandmother of which famous king of Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ruth's line led through Obed and Jesse to King David.

quizQuestions.prompt: During what period in Israel's history does the book of Ruth take place?
quizQuestions.explanation: The story of Ruth unfolds during the time the judges ruled.

quizQuestions.prompt: Where did Boaz legally finalize his right to redeem Ruth and marry her, in front of witnesses?
quizQuestions.explanation: Boaz settled the matter at the city gate, the customary place for legal business.
